label: The Pulse
desc: One note per click. Nothing else.
tip: Count out loud: ONE, two, three, four. Aim to make the click disappear underneath your note — when you are dead on, you stop hearing it.

label: Eighths, Held
desc: Two to a beat, all the way through.
tip: Count "1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &" out loud without stopping. The second half of each beat is where evenness is won or lost.

label: Eighths
desc: Quarters and pairs of eighths — the first split of the beat.
tip: Count "1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &" out loud, all the way through, even where you play nothing.

label: Rests & Syncopation
desc: Silence on the beat, notes off it. Where you DON'T play is the exercise.
tip: Keep counting through the rests. A rest is a note you play with your silence — it still has to be in time.

label: Sixteenths, Held
tip: Count "1 e & a". Most players squeeze the "a" — watch the error meter and find out whether that is you.

label: Sixteenths
desc: Four to a beat, plus the dotted figures that live between them.
tip: Count "1 e & a". Most players rush the "a" — watch the error meter and see if that is you.

label: Triplets
desc: Three to a beat — a different grid entirely, not a swung version of the last one.
tip: Count "1 trip let, 2 trip let". The trap is leaning triplets toward sixteenths; the middle note is the giveaway.

label: Thirty-seconds, Held
desc: Eight to a beat. The tempo ceiling arrives fast, and honestly.
tip: At this density the game caps the tempo where it can still hear each attack separately. Start slow: evenness first, speed after.

label: Subdivision Ladder
desc: Same tempo, climbing divisions: quarters → eighths → triplets → sixteenths, and back down.
tip: The tempo never changes — only how finely you split it. Keep the click in exactly the same place in your body as the rungs go by.

label: Tresillo
desc: 3-3-2. The one-bar cell underneath half the world's music.
tip: Feel it as long-long-short, not as counted sixteenths. Once it locks, it stops feeling like maths.

label: Backbeat: 2 & 4
desc: The metronome clicks only on 2 and 4. You supply 1 and 3.
tip: Hear the click as the snare, not the beat. If it starts drifting to sound like 1 and 3, stop and reset — that flip is the whole test.

label: Offbeat Click
desc: The click lands on every "&". You play the downbeats against it.
tip: Hardest sound in the room. Sing the downbeats before you play them; if the click ever flips into feeling like the beat, you have lost it.

label: Gap Click
desc: Two bars of metronome, two bars of nothing. Keep going through the silence.
tip: Victor Wooten's drill. The click coming back is the exam: if it lines up, your internal clock is real. Don't speed up in the gap — almost everyone does.
